modules.intro: The template gives you a 2.000 in square. Everything you draw lives inside it. The only thing that matters today is that your shape closes.
modules.title: Sketch the Outline
modules.aiNote: AI is a tutor here, not a source: it can walk you through a tool or explain why something is not working, but the shape has to be yours. Press Win plus Shift plus S to capture part of your screen, paste it straight into an AI chat, and ask what to do next.

blocks.content:
1. Download **dogtag_template.SLDPRT** from this assignment and open it in SolidWorks.
2. In the FeatureManager design tree, right-click **Starter Sketch** and choose **Edit Sketch**.
3. You will see a square perimeter, 2.000 in on a side. Your design stays inside it.
4. Use line, arc, circle, and trim to build the outer shape of your tag. It has to end as one closed loop with no gaps.
5. Add a circle for the chain hole. **No dimensions today.** Leave enough material between the hole and the outside edge that it reads like a real dogtag.
6. Exit the sketch.

Sketch tools, relations, dragging, and trimming are in the **CAD Quick Reference**. So is **Getting Unstuck**, which shows you how to screenshot what you are looking at and ask an AI what to do next. Use it. Do not sit and wait.

levels.label: Complete
levels.descriptor: The outline is one closed loop with no gaps, no overlapping ends, and no leftover or stray entities inside the perimeter.

levels.label: Proficient
levels.descriptor: The outline is one closed loop, with one or two stray entities left behind in the sketch.

levels.label: Developing
levels.descriptor: The outline has a visible gap or overlapping ends at one location.

levels.label: Absent
levels.descriptor: No outline drawn, or the outline is open at more than one location.

levels.label: Complete
levels.descriptor: The hole is a closed circle set in from the outline with material visible all the way around it, and the entire design sits inside the square perimeter.

levels.label: Developing
levels.descriptor: The hole is closed but nearly touches the outline, or the hole is not closed, or part of the design crosses the square perimeter.

levels.label: Absent
levels.descriptor: No hole drawn.

modules.intro: SolidWorks made the geometry. The DXF is how that geometry gets handed to the laser. Check it before you leave SolidWorks, because a bad DXF is invisible until it is too late.
modules.title: Extrude and Export the DXF
modules.aiNote: Use AI to get unstuck on the export wizard, not to decide anything for you. Pasting a screenshot of the dialog into the chat and asking what each option does is faster than describing it in words.

blocks.content:
1. Features tab, **Boss Extrude**. Type **0.100 in** and confirm.
2. Save the part to **[FOLDER PATH]**.
3. Click the flat face of your tag to select it.
4. **File, Save As**, navigate to **[FOLDER PATH]**, and set the file type to **DXF**.
5. The export wizard picks up the face you already selected. Step through it and finish.
6. Before you move on, confirm the DXF is **one closed outline with one hole**, nothing else.

items: Part file saved to the class folder
DXF file saved to the class folder

levels.label: Complete
levels.descriptor: The part is extruded and saved, and the exported DXF opens in xTool Studio showing the outline and the hole as two closed paths at the size drawn in SolidWorks.

levels.label: Proficient
levels.descriptor: The DXF opens with the outline and hole both present, but at a size that does not match the SolidWorks sketch.

levels.label: Developing
levels.descriptor: The DXF opens with geometry missing, or with more than the flat face exported.

levels.label: Absent
levels.descriptor: No extrude performed, or no DXF produced, or the file does not open.

modules.intro: SolidWorks makes geometry. xTool Studio makes a machine job. Same shape, different question: this is where you decide what the laser actually does to each line. You are not running the machine. Your saved file goes into a batch that gets cut before Monday.
modules.title: Set Up the Job in xTool Studio
modules.aiNote: AI can explain what cut, score, and engrave do and where things live in xTool Studio. What goes on your tag and which process each feature gets are your calls, and you have to be able to explain them.

blocks.content:
1. Open **xTool Studio** and click **New Project**.
2. On the right side of the screen, set the machine to **xTool MetalFab**.
3. Click the **plus** icon on the right and import your DXF.
4. Use the **text tool** to add your name. School appropriate only.
5. You may also add an image. What engraves well and what does not is in the **CAD Quick Reference**.
6. Assign **cut**, **score**, or **engrave** to every feature. Cut belongs on the outline and the hole, nothing else.
7. Click **Process** in the bottom right to preview the toolpath. Check it.
8. Save the project file to **[FOLDER PATH]**.

items: xTool project file saved to the class folder

levels.label: Complete
levels.descriptor: Name plus at least one added element, text or image, is placed, and every added element sits fully inside the outline.

levels.label: Developing
levels.descriptor: A name is placed with nothing else added, or an added element crosses or touches the outline.

levels.label: Absent
levels.descriptor: Nothing added to the imported shape.

levels.label: Complete
levels.descriptor: Every feature carries a process, with cut assigned to the outline and the hole and score or engrave assigned to everything added.

levels.label: Proficient
levels.descriptor: Every feature carries a process, but cut is assigned to a feature other than the outline or the hole.

levels.label: Developing
levels.descriptor: One or more features carry no process.

levels.label: Absent
levels.descriptor: No processes assigned, or the machine was never set to xTool MetalFab.

modules.intro: Your file goes to the machine without you. Everything the laser does to your tag is already decided by what you just saved.
modules.title: Hand Off the File
modules.aiNote: AI can help you understand what you are seeing in the preview. The answer is your own reading of your own file, so do not have it written for you.

blocks.prompt: You are handing this file off and you will not be there when it cuts. From your Process preview, state what the laser will do to your outline, to your hole, and to one thing you added. Then name one thing that could still go wrong.

levels.label: Complete
levels.descriptor: Names the process assigned to the outline, to the hole, and to one added feature, and names one specific thing that could go wrong on this tag.

levels.label: Developing
levels.descriptor: Names the process for only some of the three features, or names all three but gives no risk, or gives a risk that is not specific to this tag.

levels.label: Absent
levels.descriptor: Not answered.

rubric.criterion: Reads the job off the preview
